description: The canonical wording of every user-facing warning and error message both SDKs emit. `template` is the canonical text; `python` and `node` are each SDK's text today, written with the same placeholders, so an SDK can see what changes. A prefix the language adds — Node's `[@stackone/ai] `, Python's logger name — is outside the template. An error's class is in `error`. `matches` says whether an SDK's text is already the canonical one; `notes` say where the text depends on more than the template.

prefixes.node: Every warning goes through console.warn, prefixed `[@stackone/ai] ` — outside the template.
prefixes.python: Every warning is a WARNING record on a `stackone.*` logger; its getMessage() is the template, rendered.

formats.json: Compact JSON text: JSON.stringify(value), json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")). A string comes out in double quotes.
formats.seconds: A number of seconds as JavaScript's String(number) writes it: 1, 0.5, 1.25 — never 1.0, never padded, never exponent form for values in [1e-6, 1e21).
formats.seconds-2dp: The seconds rounded half up to two decimals, Math.floor(x * 100 + 0.5) / 100, then written as `seconds`: 0, 0.75, 1.5.
formats.json-type: The JSON type of the value: object, array, string, number, boolean or null.
formats.reason: The text for a header reason code, from `reasons`.

reasons.not-a-scalar: not a string, number or boolean

messages.template: Every account failed to list tools: {failures}

failures.description: each failed account as "{account_id}: {error}", where {error} is the failure's own message (as in skip-account), in ascending account-id order, joined by "; " — e.g. "acc-1: <message>; acc-2: <message>"

messages.python: Every account failed to list tools: {failures}
messages.node: Every account failed to list tools: {failures}
messages.notes: Only when every account in scope failed to list, and only when the failures do not all share one HTTP status: if they do, the SDK rethrows the StackOneAPIError itself (e.g. two accounts both answering 401 raise StackOneAPIError 401). The failures are the error's cause: Python raises it `from ExceptionGroup(...)` of them, Node passes `{ cause: new AggregateError(...) }`. An account that listed zero tools has not failed. Both SDKs join the failures with "; ", and also raise when some accounts failed and the rest listed zero tools. Replaces no-account-returned-tools.
